name: Redirect to user-controlled URL (gin / net/http open redirect)
attack_scenario: Victim clicks https://trusted.app/login?next=https://evil.example/login, authenticates, and is bounced to the attacker's pixel-perfect clone that harvests the just-entered credentials.
negative_test_hint: request /login?next="https://evil.example.com/login" and assert the redirect target is rejected or rewritten to a same-site relative path

exemplar.explanation: Passing a request-derived value straight into gin's c.Redirect or net/http's http.Redirect lets an attacker choose the Location header, a classic open redirect that makes phishing links look like they originate from your trusted domain. Redirect targets must be validated to a same-site relative path (leading single '/', never '//') or an explicit allowlist.
